title: Two-parameter single-molecule analysis for measurement of chromatin mobility
protocol: Incubate cells with 5 nM fluorescent Halo ligand JF549 for 15 minutes.
Remove the medium containing excess fluorophore.
Replace with fresh medium free of Phenol Red.
Repeat the removal and replacement of medium three times.
Leave the cells in the incubator for 15 minutes to release unbound fluorophore.
Remove the medium again.
Replace with fresh medium free of phenol red.
Detect JF549 fluorescence using a laser with peak excitation at 549 nm.
Set initial laser power and exposure time to moderate settings of 100 ms.
Adjust focus and illumination angle for optimal signal quality.
Take a snapshot of the nucleus/nuclei to be analyzed.
Set camera exposure time to 10 ms.
Progressively increase laser power until single molecules become visible.
Photobleach the nucleus if necessary, which may take several seconds.
Adjust illumination angle, z-axis position, and laser power for optimal molecule density and background-to-signal ratio.
Photobleach the nucleus to visualize single molecules and optimize background-to-signal ratio.
Record single-molecule tracking data starting as soon as possible after photobleaching.
Typically, record 5,000 frames (total acquisition duration: 50 s).
Start MATLAB and run SLIMFast.m.
In SLIMfast, hit Load > Batch, and select the .tif stacks to analyze.
Adjust the Optics parameters in SLIMfast: set fluorophore emission for JF549=580 nm, objective numerical aperture (NA), and camera pixel size used during single-molecule imaging.
Add the tracking script package to the path.
Detect molecules in successive frames of the .tif single-molecule imaging stacks.
Load particle data using SLIMfast > Particle data and select an individual .mat file.
Display an overlay of all particles detected over the course of acquisition.
Hit OPT > Tracking, and change the Max. expected Diffusion Coefficient to 3 μm²/s in the overlay menu.
Hit “GEN TRAJ” in the overlay window to track molecules frame-by-frame.
Save output files in the directory of choice once processing is completed.
Discard trajectories shorter than 5 frames to optimize classification.
Compute the T-MSD curve for each individual trajectory.
Fit each full T-MSD curve with a power law distribution.
Classify trajectories based on α values: α≤0.7 as confined, 0.7<α<1 as Brownian, and α≥1 as directed.
Detect "Butterfly" trajectories with mixed behaviors based on displacement criteria.
Split Butterfly trajectories into confined and Directed/Brownian segments using geometrical properties.
Classify confined trajectories based on their average frame-to-frame displacement.
Consider trajectories with an average displacement below 100 nm as confined, indicating molecules interacting with chromatin.
Gather the batch of .txt files generated by SLIMfast.m into a unique folder.
Run csv_converter.m to convert each .txt file into a .csv file.
Select the batch of tracking .csv files to analyze in SMT_Motion_Classifier.m.
Measure the radius of confinement and the average displacement for single molecules.
Run the Two_Parameter_SMT.m script on nuclear protein trajectories in a chromatin-bound state.
Define confined trajectories as those below the jump threshold (confined_Low_Jump_0.1).
Include the confined portion of butterfly trajectories (Butterfly_segments_confined) in the analysis.
Fit individual T-MSD curves with a circle confined diffusion model to measure the radius of confinement.
Calculate the average displacement by measuring the Euclidean distance between consecutive positions in the motion track.
Generate a scatter plot of the radius of confinement versus average displacement for 80,000 individual trajectories.
Run Two_Parameter_MSD and hit “add.”
Go to the appropriate directory and open Butterfly_segments_confined.mat and confined_Low_jump_0.1.mat for the set of data to analyze.
Hit “Done Selecting Files” and wait for the script to execute.
Measure local density in different chromatin mobility populations using scatplot.m.
Normalize density values by the maximum density value for each condition.
Compute density differences between the protein of interest and the reference by subtracting the average density of the five nearest points from the density of each trajectory of interest.
Multiply the result by −1 for intuitiveness.
Generate 3 output plots using the script: one individual density plot for the reference and another for the protein of interest.
Create a histogram plot displaying average and standard error across 4 mobility populations.
Exclude the very high mobility population due to sparse data causing measurement errors.
On line 9 of the Density_differences.m script, specify the number of trajectories to analyze.
Recommend running the script on n ≥ 10,000 randomly downsampled data points.
Run the Density_differences.m script and select trackingdata.xlsx for the reference plot first.
Select trackindata.xlsx file for the protein of interest next.
Save the generated figures in the desired format.
